sentences.text: Joydeep Nath vs Unknown on 11 December, 2019

Author: Suvra Ghosh
Bench: Suvra Ghosh

1

11.12.2019
(Pp) Crr 2704 of 2019 In the matter of : Joydeep Nath ....petitioner Mr. Debasish Roy, Mr.
Sandipan Ganguly, Mr. Vivek Jhunjhunwalla, Mr. Anirban Tarafder ....for the petitioner.
Mr. Anindya Sundar Chatterjee, Mr. Goutam Dinda ....for the opposite party.

The petitioner in the present revisional application challenges the order dated 25th March, 2019 passed by the learned 3rd Metropolitan and Municipal Magistrate, Kolkata, in connection with Complaint Case No. 6D of 2010 under Sections 16(1)(a)(i) read with Section 12/7 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

It is submitted on behalf of the petitioner that the petitioner filed an application before the learned Trial Court under Section 205 of the Code of Criminal Procedure seeking permission to be represented through his learned advocate.
The said petition was turned down by the learned Trial Court, against which the petitioner preferred revision.

In disposing of the revisional application, the learned revisional Court directed the learned Magistrate to rehear the petition under section 205 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and to pass appropriate order.
The petition was moved afresh before the learned Trial Court and by the impugned order, the learned Trial Court rejected the said application.
The learned advocate for the petitioner has referred to a photocopy of a document which suggests that the petitioner is the Director of several companies.
In opposing the prayer of the petitioner, the opposite party submits that allowing an application under Section 205 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is the discretionary power of the Court.

In fact,
no serious objection was raised by the opposite party against the petition under Section 205 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

It is envisaged in Section 205(1) of the Code that - "Whenever a Magistrate issues a summons, he may, if he sees reason so to do,

1 dispense with the personal attendance of the accused and permit him to appear by his pleader."

sentences.text: In the present case, it prima facie appears that the petitioner is a Director of several companies and it is the case of the petitioner that he has to travel extensively due to his business commitments.
The petitioner has also undertaken not to dispute his identity as the accused of the case and also not to challenge the evidence recorded by the Court in his absence.

In view of the undertaking given by the petitioner in the application under Section 205 of the Code and also in view of the professional engagement of the petitioner, I am inclined to hold that the petitioner should be permitted to be represented in the case before the learned Trial Court through his pleader and his personal attendance before the learned Trial Court may be dispensed with.
It is made clear that the learned Trial Court shall be at liberty to direct the personal attendance of the petitioner if the circumstances of the case so demand, in accordance with law.
C.R.R. 2704 of 2019 is allowed accordingly.
Personal attendance of the petitioner before the learned Trial Court is dispensed with and the petitioner is permitted to be represented before the Court through his pleader.
Urgent certified website copies of this order, if applied for, be made available to the parties upon compliance with the requisite formalities.

(Suvra Ghosh, J.)
